newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy VAT receipts down 6.5 pct in Jan-Feb - report.
newsitem.headline: Italy VAT receipts down 6.5 pct in Jan-Feb - report.

text.p: Receipts from value added taxes (VAT) fell a gross 6.5 percent year-on-year in Italy in the first two months of the year, former finance minister Giulio Tremonti said at the weekend, quoting official documents.
He said VAT from internal trade fell 8.0 percent. "This is the real indication of the health of companies," Tremonti told reporters at a convention in the north of Italy on Saturday.
Overall, returns from indirect taxation rose 0.5 percent in January and February to 23.2 trillion lire from 23.1 trillion lire for the same period last year, Tremonti added.
A spokesman for the finance ministry said tax receipts so far this year were "perfectly in line with forecasts."

Tremonti was quoted in Italian newspapers as saying the tax data was normally ready for publication 45 days after the month in question had ended and called on the government to release the full figures immediately.
He added that receipts from instant scratch lottery cards collapsed 30.7 percent in January and February against the same period in 1996.
Tremonti served as finance minister in Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right administration in 1994.
